sources.title: RIL financial reporting and Q1 FY2027 highlights
Reliance current P/E and historical valuation comparison
Reliance valuation and refinery-marketing peer metrics
India asks private fuel retailers to end sales rationing
Strong institutional demand for Reliance rupee bond issue

claims.statement: RIL's Q1 FY27 gross revenue was about Rs 3.40 lakh crore, EBITDA about Rs 54,067 crore and PAT about Rs 23,196 crore; management reported strong O2C and Jio performance and a healthy balance sheet, supporting a positive fundamental direction.

June 2026 data show FII/FPI ownership falling from 18.67% to 17.19% and total institutional ownership from 39.30% to 38.46%, although mutual-fund ownership rose from 9.78% to 10.11%; on balance the institutional direction is negative.

The government directive to end fuel-sales rationing creates a negative near-term catalyst for Reliance's domestic fuel-retailing economics, partly offset by strong demand for its recent AAA-rated bond issue; the more immediate operating catalyst is assessed negative.

RIL traded near 21.15x earnings, below its own 5-year P/E near 25.36x but at a substantial premium to many refinery/marketing peers; because the governed valuation comparison is sector-relative, the current valuation direction is assessed negative with conglomerate-comparison limitations noted.

India's oil ministry said private fuel retailers including Reliance would be asked to stop rationing diesel and gasoline while regulated retail prices remain below market economics; this is a verified moderate negative event-risk signal.

limitations: Research was freshly executed for this distinct G5.1 acceptance run; no prior bundle was merely retimestamped or reused.
VERIFIED_NEUTRAL is used only where current evidence was actively checked and no material directional signal was established.
Valuation conclusions are contextual and do not replace the frozen provider score; independent research validates, conflicts with or excludes provider interpretation under governed reconciliation.
